## Expression on this line

Needs at Stage 1 is **system-maintenance without felt need**: the molecular substrate that persists through thermodynamic gradient, maintaining its structure not because it "needs" to but because the physical conditions permit it. There is no "need" in any psychological sense — no hunger, no thirst, no desire, no want. There is only the physical fact that some configurations of matter persist and others dissolve. The "need" at Stage 1 is a *thermodynamic* need: the system requires free energy to maintain its structure against entropy, but this requirement is not experienced by the system. It is a need without a needer.

The proto-motivational significance of Stage 1 is that it establishes the *infrastructure of persistence*: the physical substrate that makes it possible for systems to maintain themselves across time. Without this thermodynamic persistence, there could be no biological needs (Stage 2+), no psychological needs (Stage 3+), no self-actualization needs (Stage 9+). ## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** proto-coherence — the "interior" of the self-organizing system; the pre-conscious ground from which felt need will eventually emerge.
- **UR:** thermodynamic persistence — the physical capacity to maintain structure against entropy; the "need" that is not felt but is real.
- **LL:** shared substrate — the common physical basis that makes system-maintenance possible.
- **LR:** thermodynamic conditions — the free energy gradient that sustains the system.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** rigid persistence — a system that maintains its structure by refusing all change; the proto-neurotic need to stay exactly as one is.
- **Dark allergy:** dissolution — the failure to maintain structure; the proto-pathological inability to sustain oneself.
- **Golden addiction:** projecting felt need onto thermodynamic persistence — treating molecular self-organization as "desire."
- **Golden allergy:** denying that thermodynamic persistence is proto-motivational — insisting that "real" needs require consciousness.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- Self-organizing chemical systems (autocatalytic sets, dissipative structures) as proto-needful systems.
- Thermodynamic gradients that sustain order as the physical substrate of all need-satisfaction.
- The boundary between living and non-living as the first proto-need distinction.

## Sources, joints, open questions

- **Sources:** Whitehead, *Process and Reality* (prehension as feeling-tone); Prigogine, *Order Out of Chaos* (dissipative structures); Deacon, *Incomplete Nature* (absential features); Maslow, *Motivation and Personality* (need hierarchy).
- **Open joints:** At what point does thermodynamic persistence become "need"? Is self-organization proto-motivational?
